correctness.rationale: The uniform-area covariance of a circumradius-one regular n-gon is ((2+cos(2*pi/n))/12) I. Thus the kernel is K_n(x,y)=1+(12/(2+cos(2*pi/n))) x dot y. Absolute kernel-row integrals are convex in x, so a vertex realizes the global norm, while rotation gives the same norm at each vertex. The unique negative cap y_1<-1/c contributes 2(-area(cap)-c first_x_moment(cap))/area(P). The polygon shoelace/cap intersection prescription covers n=3, even and odd n and boundary clipping. A radial expansion r_n(phi)=cos(pi/n)/cos(s) gives mean delta r=-pi^2/(3n^2); the derivative of the disk integral yields 5*pi*sqrt(15)/12, with a Lipschitz error term controlling the angular microstructure. Reconstructed cap formula independently from clipping: triangle=19/8, square=233/108, hexagon=361/180 to machine precision, and rescaled corrections 5.07083 (n=80), 5.06974 (n=320), 5.069727 (n=500) approach 5.0697233. Finite checks support but do not prove the n->infinity limit. The proof supplies all quantifiers and the needed radial remainder.

value.rationale: Filled regular polygons are a canonical geometric approximation of the disk, and the degree-one L2 projector is the natural least-squares stability baseline. The all-n sharp endpoint constants and signed n^-2 correction answer a motivated domain-approximation question beyond arbitrary numerical cases; triangle/square/disk special cases alone would not qualify.

limitations: A full archival survey of weighted polynomial projection constants on polygonal domains was not possible; a differently phrased exact formula could exist.
The radial asymptotic is proved analytically; finite n checks alone would not establish the coefficient.
No monotonicity in n or optimum over all polygons is claimed.
